RIBBED FLAT AT LOW TIDE: a great sheet of ribbed wet sand holding a pewter mirror sheen, shallow runnels braiding toward a low sandbar at the sea's edge, a kelp line strung with shells along the tideline, a weathered rowboat upturned near the dune foot with barnacles crusting its keel, a headland stepping away into haze far off.

SANDBAR AND RUNNELS: a wide low-tide flat of pale gold ribbed sand, runnels threading between two exposed sandbars, foam lines sliding back across the near bar, a rusted anchor half-buried at the tideline, a second sandbar catching jade water beyond, the open sea flattening to slate blue at the horizon.

KELP-LINE BEACH: a broad wet-sand flat combed with current ripples, a thick kelp line draped along the tideline in ribbons of olive and amber, a driftwood shelter built and left above the strandline, shallow runnels catching a sheen of turquoise, a distant headland curling like a sleeping cat into the far sea.

SHELL-SCATTERED FLAT: a wide arc of ribbed sand at the lowest tide pocked with shell clusters and pebble patches, a stout weathered timber marker post hung with a life ring standing tall at mid-distance on the flat, shallow swell lines feathering over a distant bar, a grassy dune ridge closing the scene landward.

DARK ROCK POOL SHELF: a broad platform of purple-grey rock pitted with round clear pools, each rim fringed in bright green weed, limpets clustered on the rims, tiny crimson anemones open inside the pools, a cairn of balanced stones on the seaward lip, long swell lines marching in beyond the shelf edge.

BLACK BASALT POOLS: a shelf of black basalt worn to an uneven natural floor, its six-sided joints softened and rounded by the sea, pools sitting in the hollows between them, weed-bearded rims, a bell hanging from a curved iron post driven into a crack, jade water foaming against the outer edge, a line of sea stacks receding into haze.

PURPLE POOL LEDGE: a tilted ledge of purple-banded rock shelving into the sea, pools sitting in the lower hollows, barnacles thick on every dry ridge, a coil of weathered rope looped around a natural bollard of rock, anemones small and brilliant inside the deepest pool, swell feathering over the outer rim.

CHALK CLIFF STEPS: soft chalk cliffs banded in cream, rose, and pale mint rising above a pebble bank graded from fist-sized to pea-sized, a crooked wooden ladder pinned to the cliff face, driftwood piled at the base, a line of smaller chalk stacks trailing seaward, foam lines stacked along the pebble shore.

BASALT COLUMN WALL: a tall headland of close-packed black basalt columns, their tops uneven and weather-rounded and crowned with wind-bent grass, a pebble-and-cobble shore at their foot, a rope swing hanging from a leaning shrub at the crest, swell lines marching in over a dark reef, spray rising at the base.

RED SANDSTONE BANDS: a cliff of red-ochre sandstone in soft uneven bands of terracotta, every band sagging and rounded by weather, the face seamed with cracks running at angles, a rock platform at its foot ribbed and pool-pitted, a tiny whitewashed hut with a blue door perched on the clifftop edge, slate-blue swell rolling in beyond the platform.

GREEN-TOPPED HEADLAND: a rounded headland of pale grey stone with a grassy crown of deep green, the cliff face stepped and pocked with ledges, a cobble and boulder shore at its foot, a string of colourful pennants strung from a post near the clifftop edge, a feathering swell line curving around the headland into the cove.

LONG PEELING WALL: a tall peeling wall of jade swell unrolling along a sandbar, its crest feathering white, a hollow tube opening at the near end, foam lines racing across the wet sand, a line of three swell ridges stacked behind the breaking wave, the near ground a sheet of ribbed sand covered in sliding foam.

SHOREBREAK FOLD: a shorebreak wave folding hard over a shallow sandbar, its lip throwing a short thick curtain of white water, foam sliding back over coarse wet sand, a second swell line gathering offshore, weathered rope tangled in the kelp line at the tideline, a low dune ridge behind.

REEF SWELL TRAIN: three swell lines marching in over a submerged reef, the nearest feathering and beginning to pitch, turquoise water between the lines, a tall barnacled rock stack standing clear of the water at mid-distance with one wind-bent tree on its crown, scattered shells on the reef flat behind.

LOW PLANK BOARDWALK: a low weathered plank boardwalk winding through sea grass to the sand, the planks silvered and salt-roughened, a stack of round lobster pots at the landward end, the boardwalk opening onto a near ground of ribbed wet sand, a headland trailing a line of stacks across the far water.

STILT WALKWAY HEADLAND: a stilt walkway curving around a rocky headland on barnacled timber piles, the planks wide and salt-worn, a life ring on a post at the midpoint, the walkway passing above a boulder shore washed by small swell, a second headland stepping into haze beyond the cove mouth.

SMALL WOODEN PIER: a small wooden pier on four rows of barnacled piles running out over pale jade shallows, its deck planks silvered and gapped, a string of colourful pennants strung along the rail, the near ground a shelf of ribbed wet sand with a sheen, swell lines rolling under the pier toward shore.

MARRAM DUNE RIDGE: rounded dune humps combed with marram grass, a sandy path cut between two humps opening onto the open turquoise sea, a fence of leaning weathered posts strung with frayed rope along one side, the near ground coarse pale sand spilling to a wet sand flat at the water's edge.

DUNE HOLLOW PATH: a deep hollow between two generous dune humps, marram and sea grass bending along the crests, a driftwood shelter tucked into the landward slope, the path opening to a ribbed sand flat with a kelp line at the tideline, a low sandbar catching pale green water beyond.

BOULDER COVE HORSESHOE: a horseshoe of rounded grey boulders cupping a small pocket of coarse golden sand, a cave arch opening in the left wall, the cove mouth showing a gap of open jade water, a cairn of balanced stones at the sand's edge, swell lines rolling through the gap and spreading into the cove.

CAVE ARCH COVE: a rocky cove with a natural arch worn through the right headland, the sea running through it in a tongue of turquoise, boulders and coarse sand on the near floor, a rusted anchor half-buried near the arch base, a second cove opening beyond the arch, swell feathering at the mouth.

TURQUOISE LAGOON FLAT: a pale shelving flat of turquoise water inside a low coral shelf, the shelf barely above the surface and fringed in coarse coral sand, leaning palms along the inner shelf, a coil of weathered rope on the sand above the tideline, the coral shelf catching white foam beyond the flat calm interior.

CORAL SAND LAGOON: a broad lagoon of banded turquoise and pale jade water held inside a coral reef shelf, coarse coral sand at the near edge grading to smooth wet sand at the water's line, a small driftwood shelter above the strand, swell lines breaking white on the outer reef, the interior water still and clear.

FAT STACK WITH TREES: a fat rounded sea stack, broad and blunt at the top, its flat top carrying a tuft of wind-bent trees, the stack a warm ochre stone with dark weed at its waterline, a pebble and cobble shore at its foot, a rounded arch worn at its base through which jade water runs, swell lines beyond.

ARCH AND OPEN SEA: a wide rounded arch worn through a pale grey headland, the sea running under it in a sheet of turquoise over a rock floor, the arch's crown mossy and dark and weather-smoothed, a rock platform at the near ground with pools in its surface, a line of smaller stacks receding into the far open sea.
